upham: Upham, N.S., Esselstyn, J.A. & Jetz, W. (2019). Inferring the mammal tree: species-level sets of phylogenies for questions in ecology, evolution, and conservation. PLoS Biology 17: e3000494. Node-dated MCC tree of the completed 5,911-species posterior (topology-constrained, birth-death); node heights and 95% HPDs
common_source: IUCN Red List 2026-1 (GBIF checklist doi:10.15468/0qnb58), preferred English name

overrides.name: Panthera
overrides.cite: Figueiró, H.V. et al. (2017). Genome-wide signatures of complex introgression and adaptive evolution in the big cats. Science Advances 3: e1700299, Fig. 1A. doi:10.1126/sciadv.1700299
overrides.reason: Upham's tree puts the snow leopard with the lion and leopard and the tiger outside the rest (2.34, 1.90 and 4.91 Ma); the genome-wide species tree (64% of windows) has tiger + snow leopard vs jaguar + (lion, leopard). Node ages and 95% HPDs are read from Fig. 1A's labels (the figure is 313 px wide, so the last digit is +-0.02; research/panthera-split-dates.md).

overrides.name: Felis catus
overrides.cite: Driscoll, C.A. et al. (2007). The Near Eastern origin of cat domestication. Science 317: 519-523. doi:10.1126/science.1139518
overrides.reason: The domestic cat is the wildcat's tamed form (from the Near Eastern wildcat), so it parts from the wildcat at domestication, not at Upham's 0.94 Ma speciation; the earliest tamed cat was buried with a person on Cyprus ~9,500 years ago (Vigne et al. 2004, Science 304: 259).

overrides.name: Panthera zdanskyi
overrides.cite: Mazák, J.H., Christiansen, P. & Kitchener, A.C. (2011). Oldest known pantherine skull and evolution of the tiger. PLoS ONE 6: e25483. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0025483
overrides.reason: The most primitive member of the tiger lineage (2.55-2.16 Ma); it branches off at its first appearance. Several later studies treat it as a synonym of P. palaeosinensis.

overrides.name: Panthera gombaszoegensis
overrides.cite: Chatar, N., Michaud, M. & Fischer, V. (2022). Not a jaguar after all? Phylogenetic affinities and morphology of the Pleistocene felid Panthera gombaszoegensis. Papers in Palaeontology 8: e1464. doi:10.1002/spp2.1464
overrides.reason: Treated as the jaguar's ancestor ("P. onca gombaszoegensis", Hemmer 1971); first appearance ~1.9-2.0 Ma (O'Regan 2002; records from ~1.5 Ma to a doubtful >2.7 Ma). Contested: the first phylogenetic analysis places it closer to the tiger. The dataset's first appearance (3.96 Ma) sits on the old crown date and is not used.

overrides.name: Panthera spelaea
overrides.cite: de Manuel, M. et al. (2020). The evolutionary history of extinct and living lions. PNAS 117: 10927-10934, SI Table S3. doi:10.1073/pnas.1919423117
overrides.reason: The cave lion's nuclear genome dates its split from the lion at 470 ka (392-529 ka; X-chromosome PSMC 495 ka, 460-578 ka). The mitogenomes give 1.89 Ma (Barnett et al. 2016).

overrides.name: Panthera balamoides
overrides.cite: Stinnesbeck, S.R. et al. (2020). Panthera balamoides and other Pleistocene felids from the submerged caves of Yucatán. Historical Biology 32: 930-939. doi:10.1080/08912963.2018.1556649
overrides.reason: Described from Yucatán caves and compared with the jaguar; it branches off the jaguar's lineage at its first appearance. Contested: Blaine et al. 2019 and Ruiz-Ramoni et al. 2019 argue it is a short-faced bear (Arctotherium).
